courses.title: Introduction to American Government (3) [GE 4B]
courses.description: [GE 4B] [AmInst-B] The study of the United States and California Constitutions and political philosophies of founders; intergovernmental relations; political institutions and processes; behavior, rights and obligations of citizens within the constraints of the institutions. Meets state requirements for American Institutions.

courses.title: Introduction to Comparative Government
courses.description: [GE 4A] Provides an introduction to the comparative study of countries’ political, economic, and social/cultural systems. Several foreign countries, both Western and non-Western, are presented as cases, to illustrate the course concepts.

courses.title: Introduction to International Relations
courses.description: [GE 4A] An introduction to international relations, with emphasis on politics among states within the international system. Introduces IR theory, the sources of foreign policy, international war, international organizations and law, and international political economy.

courses.title: Introduction to Political Thought
courses.description: [GE 3B] Outlines the major political philosophers and their contributions to political thinking around making a humane and just society possible. Explains central concepts such as justice, sovereignty, natural rights, democracy, power, equality, capitalism, humanism, knowledge, and freedom, and their implications for addressing important political and moral questions. Engages canonical and non-canonical authors and texts from the ancient period to the 21st century to critically examine the development of these concepts across varying historical contexts and civilizations.

courses.title: Research Methods
courses.description: Focus on practical skills for conducting empirical research. The basics for searching scholarly material, utilizing research designs, hypothesis formation, hypothesis testing, and qualitative research methods.

courses.title: Introduction to Public Administration
courses.description: Introduction to field of public administration for students interested in pursuing a career in government. Focus on structures, functions, principles, and processes of administration in American public sector. Attention to the core functions of public administration, and basic skills required in managing and leading public organizations.

courses.title: Introduction to Public Law
courses.description: Provides a basic understanding of public law’s theoretical and historical foundation, and its functioning within legislative, judicial and administrative institutions of government.

courses.title: Introduction to Race and Ethnic Politics
courses.description: [GE 6] Cross Listed as: EWS 2080 Minority communities, citizenship, political values, attitudes, behaviors, and policy issues and representation in the United States. Emphasis on the experience of Native Americans, African Americans, Asian Americans, and/or Latina and Latino Americans, along with the overall immigrant experience in the US.

courses.title: The American Congress
courses.description: The examination of the inner workings of the United States Congress; compare and contrast the House of Representatives and the Senate; understanding the policymaking process; compare and contrast the institution with other legislative bodies.

courses.title: The American Presidency
courses.description: The role of the presidency within the federal political system: behavior, processes and functions. Emphasis on constitutional underpinnings and institutionalization of the American presidency, on other executive components and on the frictions created by competing values in the administrative process.

courses.title: The American Judiciary
courses.description: Courts as political subsystems, the structure of the federal judiciary; the nature and scope of judicial power; the Supreme Court and American political development; the politics of judicial appointment; influences on judicial decision making; state court appointment.

courses.title: Asian American Politics
courses.description: [GE 6] Cross Listed as: EWS 3275 Provides an interdisciplinary overview of Asian American politics to learn about how and why different Asian American communities have been politically engaged throughout history and across different policy issues. Addresses the relationship between the racialization of Asian Americans and their political engagement. Topics covered include labor, immigration, citizenship, education, environmental justice, and civil rights. In addition to analyzing the different types of political engagement and activism of the different communities that define Asian America, the intersections of identities and coalition-building within the broader panethnic Asian American community and across other racialized groups are also examined. Critically analysis of course materials to expand upon understandings of Asian Americans and challenge dominant tropes and norms of political participation and leadership.

courses.title: Race and Ethnic Politics in the United States
courses.description: Contemporary political experience of racial and ethnic groups; investigation of strategies used in navigating American politics; interpretation of class struggle and its relationship to ethnicity and politics; and importance of political organizations and mobilization.

courses.title: American Political Institutions and Behavior (3) [GE 4C]
courses.description: [GE 4C] [AmInst-B] The study of institutions and political behavior, the evolution and understanding of citizens’ preference in a federated Constitution, the importance of institutions that communicate citizen opinions and preferences, and particular focus on the California experience. Course also fulfills American Institutions Graduation Requirement: U.S. Constitution and California Government (Part B).
courses.prerequisites: Junior or senior standing; and completion of GE Areas 1 and 2, or Areas A and B4 are recommended.

courses.title: Voting and Elections in the United States
courses.description: Examination of electoral processes and outcomes; Assessment of voting behavior, especially regarding democratic theory and implications for representation; Attention to political actors: politicians, lobbyists, activists, and political donors; and an analysis of factors influencing public opinion and political participation.

courses.title: Public Opinion
courses.description: Study of character, formation, and nature of public opinion: the construction of beliefs and attitudes; role of public opinion in elections; stability of opinions and voter psychology; the public’s political sophistication; and growth of alienation.

courses.title: Women and Politics in America
courses.description: The role of gender of political behavior, attitudes, and opinions in the United States. Focus on women’s participation in the political process since the founding, the Suffrage Movement, and contemporary politics. Focuses on the role women play as voters, activists, and political elites.

courses.title: Political Communication and Media
courses.description: Study of media as political institution including: analysis of communications and its effects; conceptualization of news and interaction with political institutions; campaign strategies and effects; and the digital media and its effect on political outcomes.

courses.title: California Government
courses.description: [GE 4C] Comparative analysis of the structures and functions of state and local governments, in California. Examination of the relationships among the several levels of government in American federalism. Course also fulfills American Institutions Graduation Requirement: U.S. Constitution and California Government (Part B) for students with AP credit in American government or U.S. government transfer credit from a University/College outside of California. Course is recommended for students who have completed 4B/D2 by AP credit (American Government) or have U.S. government transfer credit from a University/College outside of California. See Advisor for additional information.
courses.prerequisites: Junior or senior standing; and completion of GE Areas 1 and 2, or Areas A and B4 are recommended.

courses.title: Applied Advocacy and Policymaking in Sacramento
courses.description: Examines the understanding of lobbying’s role in government to produce meaningful policy change. Understanding of effective lobbying practices, framing advocacy messages, coordinating meetings with elected officials.

courses.title: Comparative Democratization
courses.description: Examines the patterns of democratization over the past few decades through major theoretical perspectives. Considers the role of domestic leaders and elites, ordinary citizens, and the international community. Also explores current challenges to democracy around the world.

courses.title: Politics of Developing Areas
courses.description: An in-depth study of economic development and underdevelopment. The focus is on extreme and moderate poverty, as well as growth in emerging economies. Theories of development, policy prescriptions, and challenges resulting from development are assessed.

courses.title: Ethnic Conflict
courses.description: Examines ethnic conflict and the role of ethnicity within modern states through major theoretical perspectives. The role of ethnicity in civil wars receives particular focus, along with policies for maintaining peace in ethnically divided societies. 3 hours lectures/discussion.

courses.title: European Governments and Politics
courses.description: Examines the political, economic, and social-cultural institutions and processes of European states and regional organizations. A comparative study of major states in the region is provided, alongside analysis of regional and contemporary challenges.

courses.title: Latin American Governments and Politics
courses.description: Examines the political, economic, and social-cultural institutions and processes of Latin American states and regional organizations. A comparative study of major states in the region is provided, alongside analysis of regional and contemporary challenges.

courses.title: Sub-Saharan African Governments and Politics
courses.description: Examines the political, economic, and social-cultural institutions and processes of sub-Saharan African states and regional organizations. A comparative study of major states in the region is provided, alongside analysis of regional and contemporary challenges.

courses.title: Middle Eastern Governments and Politics
courses.description: Examines the political, economic, and social-cultural institutions and processes of Middle Eastern states and regional organizations. A comparative study of major states in the region is provided, alongside analysis of regional and contemporary challenges.

courses.title: Government and Politics of the Russian Federation
courses.description: Examines the political, economic, and social-cultural institutions and processes of Russian Federation states and regional organizations. A primary focus on Russia is provided, alongside analysis of regional and contemporary challenges.

courses.title: East Asian Governments and Politics
courses.description: Examines the political, economic, and social-cultural institutions and processes of East Asian states and regional organizations. A comparative study of major states in the region is provided, alongside analysis of regional and contemporary challenges.

courses.title: Southeast Asian Governments and Politics
courses.description: Examines the political, economic, and social-cultural institutions and processes of Southeast Asian states and regional organizations. A comparative study of major states in the region is provided, alongside analysis of regional and contemporary challenges.

courses.title: US Foreign Policy
courses.description: In-depth study of US Foreign Policy, focusing on its domestic sources, including government agencies, interest groups, and public opinion, its historical eras, including the ideologies and key turning points among them, and current challenges.

courses.title: International Political Economy
courses.description: In-depth study of international political economy, both the political basis of economic action and the economic basis of political action. Studying the origins and structure of the global economy as well as current issues.

courses.title: International War and Peace
courses.description: An in-depth study of international war, including conventional and guerrilla war. Topics include theories of war, modern weaponry, war as a function of foreign policy, the changing nature of war, guerrilla warfare, and counterinsurgency strategy.

courses.title: International Law
courses.description: In-depth study of international law, focusing on its sources, function, and evolution. Particular focus on principal law-making and adjudicatory agencies, diplomatic relations, treaties and executive agreements, settlement of disputes, and the laws of war.

courses.title: Environmental Security
courses.description: Focuses on problems transcending international boundaries which are not state-centric, including problems with populations, health, food, climate, energy, water, and more. Emphasis is on interdependence, collective goods, sustainability, and contrasts between wealthy and poor populations.

courses.title: Terrorism
courses.description: Examines the problem of terrorism, including its definition, origins and development, cases of terrorist organizations, its expansion into a global phenomenon, tactics and strategies, the question of causes, and counterterrorism’s tactics, strategies, and policy dilemmas.

courses.title: Transnational Crime
courses.description: Study of transnational criminal industries focusing on drugs, weapons, human smuggling, and other illicit industries, including money laundering. Additional focus on the role of laws, policies, and social norms in shaping and countering illicit industries.

courses.title: Ancient and Medieval Political Thought
courses.description: Major contributions of Plato and Aristotle to Western political philosophy; survey of the Middle Ages. Emphasis on the timeliness of classical and medieval political conceptions.

courses.title: Modern Political Thought
courses.description: Analysis of the major thinkers and questions of the modern period from the Renaissance to the 19th century.

courses.title: American Political Thought
courses.description: Major ideas and thinkers who have influenced American political life through the 19th century.

courses.title: Feminist Political Theory
courses.description: Cross Listed as: NA Dual Listed as: NA Expands what is meant by “political theory” by giving critical attention to the “woman’s” experience and its relationship to “truth” and knowledge, the role of language in feminist liberatory projects, and the goal of equality. Surveys various feminist interventions in political thought from the 18th century to the present (liberal, socialist, Marxist, radical, postmodern, etc.) to interrogate normative political theory and its (in)attention to patriarchy and its relationship to other core concepts in contemporary political thought (e.g., capitalism, white supremacy, colonialism). Expands what is meant by “feminist” by centering Women of Color and intersectional feminist rejoinders to each of the “classic” schools of feminist political thought. Special attention is given to questions of feminist methodology in preparation for a major feminist political theory research project.
courses.prerequisites: Students should have achieved upper-division status. No prerequisites are required, but PLS 2040 and EWS 3900 are both strongly recommended.

courses.title: Advanced American Political Thought
courses.description: An analysis of the major ideas and thinkers of the twentieth century who have influenced American political life.

courses.title: Contemporary Political Theory
courses.description: An analysis of the major ideas and thinkers who have influenced contemporary political theory in the 20th and 21st centuries.

courses.title: Coalitional Activism: Women of Color Feminist Interventions
courses.description: Cross Listed as: NA Dual Listed as: NA Uses a semester-long coalition simulation to explore the modes of activism conducive to pursuing intersectional social justice. Centers Women of Color feminist interventions into discussions around coalition politics and coalitional solidarity within contemporary political theory (and especially in response to Judith Butler’s work in this area). In so doing, it examines the origins of intersectionality as a lens for making sense of interlocking oppressive forces, the notions of feminist subjectivity and consciousness necessary for successful coalescing, the possibilities and challenges of political solidarity across race, class, sexuality, gender, and other divides, the relationship between ethics and politics in the space of intersectional coalitions, and the process of collective authorship in the service of intersectional liberation. Offers a polytechnic experience through a semester-long coalition simulation, wherein students will put into practice coalitional theories introduced to them across the semester and collectively author one of the core empirical “texts” of the course through a weekly coalition journal.
courses.prerequisites: Junior or senior standing. PLS 3345 and/or EWS 4400 strongly recommended.
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times Minimum - Maximum Units: Total credit limited to 6 units, with a maximum of 3 units per semester.

courses.title: Environmental Political Theory
courses.description: An analysis of the major ideas and thinkers who have influenced the way nature and the environment is understood and treated in the economy, politics, and society.

courses.title: Politics of Public Policy
courses.description: The politics of the policy process; the examination of public policy in relation to democratic institutions; the making of public policy responsive to democratic control; and issues of diversity and impact of changing demographics on the policy agenda.

courses.title: Urban Administration, Politics and Policy
courses.description: Examines urban development and politics; addresses basic concepts of institutions, procedures and politics; discusses policy issues of urban sprawl, transportation, and public schools; and debates on reforms of urban governance. The changing approaches to governance, administration and policies are explored.

courses.title: NGOs and Social Service Outreach
courses.description: Non-governmental organization history, theories, concepts; governmental inefficiency; social service outreach; the need for NGOs; capacity building; leadership; responding to crises; the international NGO perspective.

courses.title: Public Organizations
courses.description: Examination of literature on organization theory and behavior generally. Emphasis on unique perspective, problems, ethical dilemmas and contributions of the public sector.

courses.title: Policy Analysis and Program Evaluation
courses.description: Introduction to policy analysis and evaluation methodology and tools used to develop and assess publicly funded programs. Systematically analyze public policies, negotiate stakeholder interests, and develop knowledge and application of policymaking concepts to address contemporary policy issues.

courses.title: The Politics of Neighborhood Change Service Learning
courses.description: Examines how neighborhoods create or inhibit social and economic opportunity, and relate to the quality of schools, streets, and institutions. Explores the role of residents, businesses, elected officials, public agencies, and policymakers in shaping neighborhood change. Covers how and why neighborhoods decline or improve, the actors that influence this process, and the contestations and collaborations that emerge among community stakeholders. As a Cal Poly Pomona service-learning course, involves significant service work in community development in the public, private, or non-profit sectors in Pomona.

courses.title: Social Capital: Theories and Applications
courses.description: Examines the various theories of social capital and how it is measured. Includes interdisciplinary research on the concept of social capital and debate over its development and usage over time. Covers the different definitions of social capital, including institutional norms, social networks, and relationships of trust. Also investigates the various benefits of social capital from labor mobility and human capital to government performance and economic stability, as well as community development and civic engagement. Emphasis on students developing their own literature review and research proposals on social capital.

courses.title: Constitutional Law: Governmental Powers
courses.description: Constitutional questions concerning the distribution of powers and responsibilities among the institutions of the federal government and between the federal and state governments. Special attentions to interbranch conflicts, constitutional crises such as the Civil War and Watergate. The course is designed for junior or senior level student majoring in political science with a concentration in public law, although it is appropriate for other students in political science, social science, or pre-law who would find the subject matter to be of interest to them. Students who are particularly inquisitive and motivated, and who are interested in developing their skills in critical analysis and writing, would derive maximum benefit from the course. The course is designed for junior or senior level student majoring in political science with a concentration in public law, although it is appropriate for other students in political science, social science, or pre-law who would find the subject matter to be of interest to them. Students who are particularly inquisitive and motivated, and who are interested in developing their skills in critical analysis and writing, would derive maximum benefit from the course.

courses.title: Constitutional Law: Rights and Liberties
courses.description: Constitutional questions arising primarily out of the 1st and 14th amendments. Supreme Court decisions regarding personal liberty; freedom of speech, press, and assembly; freedom of and from religion; and equal protection of the laws. The course is designed for junior or senior level student majoring in political science with a concentration in public law, although it is appropriate for other students in political science, social science, or pre-law who would find the subject matter to be of interest to them. courses.title: Constitutional Law: Criminal Justice
courses.description: Constitutional questions concerning the operation of the criminal justice process in the United States. Special attention will be given to the Federal system’s impact on state criminal justice systems.

courses.title: The Criminal Justice System
courses.description: Criminal justice administration concepts, institutions; relationship to legislative functions and issues; interagency and intergovernmental collaboration; politics of crime, Constitutional issues, ethics, white collar crime, prison reform, rehabilitation, and re-entry issues.

courses.title: Jurisprudence
courses.description: The nature and sources of law; the process of legal interpretation; the meaning of legal concepts like justice, liberty, responsibility, negligence, punishment.

courses.title: Contemporary Issues in American Law
courses.description: In-depth analysis of current debates and controversies in or about American law and legal studies; topics will be specified in advance.

courses.title: Model United Nations
courses.description: [GE 3C or 4C] Exclusively for students who have applied, and been accepted, to CPP’s Model United Nations team. Serves as preparation for the team’s annual Model UN conferences.
courses.prerequisites: Junior or senior standing; and completion of GE Areas 1 and 2, or Areas A and B4 are recommended.
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times Minimum - Maximum Units: Total credit limited to 12 units.

courses.title: Judicial Internship
courses.description: Observation of a variety of court sessions in the Los Angeles Superior Court system, including criminal, civil, juvenile, mental health, family law. Students meet with judges and lawyers at the courts and other offices of the legal system.

courses.title: Judicial Internship Activity
courses.description: Observation of a variety of court sessions in the Los Angeles Superior Court system, including criminal, civil, juvenile, mental health, family law. Students meet with judges and lawyers at the courts and other offices of the legal system.

courses.title: Study Abroad: International Fieldwork
courses.description: [GE 3C or 4C] Study Abroad; history, language, culture, politics, of international destinations; the past, present, future of international destination; comparative perspectives.
courses.prerequisites: Junior or senior standing; and completion of GE Areas 1 and 2, or Areas A and B4 are recommended.

courses.title: Mock Trial
courses.description: Development of oral and written presentations in response to case studies on contemporary legal controversies. Preparation for regional and Mock Trial competitions.

courses.title: Mock Trial Activity
courses.description: Development of oral and written presentations in response to case studies on contemporary legal controversies. Preparation for regional and Mock Trial competitions. May be taken up to six times for a total credit of 6 units.

courses.title: Politics, Policies, Pop Culture
courses.description: [GE 4C] Popular culture concepts; mass media, race, gender, class, sexuality; legislative actions, regulating youth and young adult behavior; regulating obscenity, the courts and popular culture, consumerism, television, movies, social media.
courses.prerequisites: Junior or senior standing; and completion of GE Areas 1 and 2, or Areas A and B4 are recommended.

courses.title: Political Campaign Management
courses.description: Explores the practice of American political campaign management, from nomination through election and in the post-campaign period. Focuses on campaign strategies and techniques and requires participation in an actual political campaign.

courses.title: Political Campaign Management Activity
courses.description: Explores the practice of American political campaign management, from nomination through election and in the post-campaign period. Focuses on campaign strategies and techniques and requires participation in an actual political campaign.

courses.title: Political Science Internship
courses.description: Selection and preparation for an internship in political science subfield. Students develop a plan for an internship opportunity related to career goals, conduct a search, apply, get selected, and work in an appropriate internship area under faculty and agency supervision.

courses.title: Political Science Internship Activity
courses.description: Selection and preparation for an internship in political science subfield. Develop a plan for an internship opportunity related to career goals, conduct a search, apply, get selected, and work in an appropriate internship area under faculty and agency supervision.

courses.title: Policies of Need and Greed
courses.description: [GE 4C] Integration of economic and political/governmental influences in the design and operation of policies regarding affluence and poverty. Market failures, government failures, and system corrections pertaining to income distribution, equity, and justice in public policy considerations in the 21st century.
courses.prerequisites: Junior or senior standing; and completion of GE Areas 1 and 2, or Areas A and B4 are recommended.
